title.narrative: Building Technical Capacity of CILSS/CERPOD for Demography in the Sahel

description.narrative: As the share of youth in their population increases, the Sahel countries are entering a critical window of opportunity when it could stand to harness historic gains: the potential of a demographic dividend, economic gains that are possible following a decline in fertility and mortality resulting in favorable child dependency ratios. However, fertility remains high in sub-Saharan Africa, but highest in the Sahel where declining mortality has not been accompanied by declining fertility as has happened in other regions. The total fertility rate is 7.6 children per woman in Niger, and the child dependency ratio is as high as 94 in Mali and 105 in Niger. The lagging demographic transition is one of the most serious developmental challenges in the region, and progress is severely constrained by regional capacity in technical knowledge, leadership and bringing about a change in political commitment on these issues. Thus, this project will support of CERPOD and National Directorates of Population (NDPs) to strengthen their capacity for technical analysis and use of evidence to inform policy dialogue; foster regional knowledge generation, exchange and consensus building on the need to reap the demographic dividend; and increase political commitment and advocacy at the highest level of government in the Sahel region. The proposed concept will focus in part on what to deliver, but there will be a strong emphasis on how to deliver it, with a key focus on using evidence, learning during implementation through a sound and functional monitoring system and effective feedback loops to make appropriate adjustments in order to achieve results. At the end of the implementation phase, success of this project will mean that at least 3 countries in the Sahel have sound national population policies based on evidence of what works best for their context, mobilized their national budgets to cofinance interventions of such policies and have a system in place to consult their constituencies (for eg online forums, facebook pages etc...) as well as learn lessons from sound monitoring systems.
